description: Required/optional field schema for Nigerian event-vendor SMEs (decor, planning, logistics for weddings, parties, corporate events). Used by parse_client_brief to detect what's present/missing in a client brief, and by generate_clarifying_questions to know which fields to ask about and how.

required_fields.label: Event Type
required_fields.description: The kind of event being planned. Drives which price-catalog items apply and how the quote is framed.
extraction_hints: Client may say 'wedding', 'owambe', 'intro/traditional wedding', 'white wedding', 'birthday party', 'send-forth', 'corporate event', 'burial', 'naming ceremony'
'Owambe' is a general Nigerian term for a lavish party — if used with no further detail, treat event_type as ambiguous and ask
clarifying_question_templates: What kind of event is this — a wedding, birthday, corporate event, or something else?
Just so I can plan properly, what's the occasion for this event?

required_fields.label: Guest Count
required_fields.description: Expected number of attendees. Primary driver of seating, catering-adjacent, and space-rental line items.
extraction_hints: Client may give a range ('100-150 people') — store as a range or take the upper bound depending on downstream pricing logic; flag ranges for the agent's reasoning notes
Vague quantifiers like 'small', 'intimate', 'plenty of people' should NOT be auto-converted to a number — treat as missing and ask for a number
clarifying_question_templates: About how many guests are you expecting?
Roughly how many people will be attending — even an estimate helps.

required_fields.label: Event Date
required_fields.description: The date (or date range) the event will take place. Drives rush-fee logic and availability messaging.
extraction_hints: Client may give relative dates ('next month', 'in 3 weeks', 'this Saturday') — resolve relative to the message's received_at timestamp where possible; if not resolvable with confidence, treat as missing and ask for a specific date
'Next month' alone (no day) should be flagged as partially missing — ask for a specific date
clarifying_question_templates: What date are you looking at for the event?
Do you have a specific date in mind, or a date range I should plan around?

required_fields.label: Venue / Location
required_fields.description: Where the event will be held (venue name, or at minimum a city/area). Affects transport/logistics contingency in pricing.
extraction_hints: Accept either a specific venue name ('Eko Hotel', 'my compound in Ikeja') or a general area if venue isn't booked yet ('somewhere in Lekki')
If client says venue is 'not yet decided,' treat this field as present but flagged 'venue_tbd: true' rather than missing — don't re-ask, note it in the quote as a placeholder assumption
clarifying_question_templates: Where will the event be held — do you have a venue yet?
What area or venue are you planning for?

required_fields.label: Budget Range
required_fields.description: Client's stated budget, exact or approximate. Used to shape which price-catalog tier the quote leans toward.
extraction_hints: Accept vague statements ('budget tight', 'nothing too expensive', 'around 500k') — vague-but-present statements should still count as 'provided' since they carry real signal; only fully absent budget mentions count as missing

'Budget tight' alone is enough to mark the field present — the agent should lean toward the lower price-catalog tier when computing the quote, not ask a follow-up unless the brief is missing everything else too
clarifying_question_templates: Do you have a budget range in mind for this?
What kind of budget are you working with, roughly?

optional_fields.label: Event Duration / Timing
optional_fields.description: How long the event runs, or start time. Affects staffing and equipment-rental duration line items.
clarifying_question_templates: What time will the event start, and about how long will it run?

optional_fields.label: Indoor or Outdoor
optional_fields.description: Affects whether canopy/tent, generator, and weather-contingency line items apply.
clarifying_question_templates: Will this be indoors, outdoors, or a mix of both?

optional_fields.label: Decor Theme / Color Scheme
optional_fields.description: Client's aesthetic preference, if any. Does not block quote generation if missing — a standard/neutral theme is assumed.
clarifying_question_templates: Do you have a color scheme or theme in mind, or should we recommend one?

optional_fields.label: Power Backup (Generator) Needed
optional_fields.description: Whether a generator/inverter is needed — common line item for Nigerian events given grid reliability. Defaults to 'yes, small unit' if venue power is uncertain and not explicitly declined.
clarifying_question_templates: Should we include backup power (generator) for the event, or does the venue already have that covered?

optional_fields.label: Catering Required
optional_fields.description: Whether the vendor should include catering in the quote, or the client is sourcing food separately. Only relevant if the SME's offering includes catering as an add-on.
clarifying_question_templates: Will you need catering included, or is that being handled separately?

optional_fields.label: Special Requirements
optional_fields.description: Anything else the client mentions unprompted — accessibility needs, religious/cultural specifics, VIP arrangements, security requests. Free text, never blocks quote generation.
clarifying_question_templates: Anything special I should know about — cultural requirements, VIP guests, accessibility needs, that sort of thing?

field_completeness_rules.notes: A brief is considered complete for compute_quote once all fields in required_for_quote are present (including 'present but flagged' states like venue_tbd or vague-budget). Optional fields never block quote generation — the agent should proceed with reasonable defaults and note any assumptions in the quote's terms.

ambiguity_handling.note: These describe guest_count in words but should not be silently converted to a number. Treat guest_count as missing and ask for an estimate, even a rough one, rather than guessing a figure that could badly skew the quote.
